question: Who has the most pole positions?
sql: SELECT drivers.driver_name, COUNT(*) AS pole_positions FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.qualifying qualifying JOIN ${catalog}.${schema}.drivers drivers ON qualifying.driver_id = drivers.driver_id WHERE qualifying.qualifying_position = 1 GROUP BY drivers.driver_name ORDER BY pole_positions DESC LIMIT 10
usage_guidance: Pole position = qualifying_position = 1 in qualifying (1994+ only).

question: Reliability / finish rate by decade
sql: SELECT decade, MEASURE(race_starts) AS race_starts, ROUND(MEASURE(finish_rate) * 100, 1) AS finish_rate_pct FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.race_performance_metrics GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY decade
usage_guidance: Use finish_rate measure for reliability / DNF questions (DNF rate = 1 - finish_rate).

question: Who was the drivers' world champion in each season?
sql: WITH final_round AS (SELECT races.year, MAX(races.round) AS last_round FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.races races JOIN ${catalog}.${schema}.driver_standings driver_standings ON driver_standings.race_id = races.race_id GROUP BY races.year) SELECT races.year, drivers.driver_name, driver_standings.points, driver_standings.wins FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.driver_standings driver_standings JOIN ${catalog}.${schema}.races races ON driver_standings.race_id = races.race_id JOIN final_round ON final_round.year = races.year AND final_round.last_round = races.round JOIN ${catalog}.${schema}.drivers drivers ON driver_standings.driver_id = drivers.driver_id WHERE driver_standings.position = 1 ORDER BY races.year DESC
usage_guidance: Championship winners come from driver_standings at the LAST round of each season, position = 1. Same pattern applies to constructor_standings.

question: Average pit stop duration by driver in 2024
sql: SELECT drivers.driver_name, COUNT(*) AS pit_stops, ROUND(AVG(pit_stops.duration_ms) / 1000, 3) AS avg_pit_stop_seconds FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.pit_stops pit_stops JOIN ${catalog}.${schema}.races races ON pit_stops.race_id = races.race_id JOIN ${catalog}.${schema}.drivers drivers ON pit_stops.driver_id = drivers.driver_id WHERE races.year = 2024 AND pit_stops.duration_ms < 60000 GROUP BY drivers.driver_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10 ORDER BY avg_pit_stop_seconds ASC LIMIT 10
usage_guidance: Pit stop duration_ms is pit-lane time (entry to exit). Exclude stops >= 60s (red-flag / repairs).

question: Top 10 drivers by number of wins, with win rate
sql: SELECT driver_name, MEASURE(wins) AS wins, MEASURE(race_starts) AS race_starts, ROUND(MEASURE(win_rate) * 100, 1) AS win_rate_pct FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.race_performance_metrics GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY wins DESC LIMIT 10
usage_guidance: Use for all-time driver rankings on wins / win rate.

question: Constructor points and wins per season for the last 5 seasons
sql: SELECT season, constructor_name, MEASURE(total_points) AS total_points, MEASURE(wins) AS wins FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.race_performance_metrics WHERE season >= (SELECT MAX(year) - 4 FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.races) GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY season, total_points DESC
usage_guidance: Use for constructor (team) comparisons across seasons.

content:
## PURPOSE
- Formula 1 analytics assistant for fans, analysts and strategists covering every World Championship season from 1950 to the current season.
- Answers questions about drivers, constructors (teams), races, circuits, championships, qualifying and pit stops.

## DISAMBIGUATION
- 'Team' means constructor. 'Season' and 'year' are the same.
- 'Champion' / 'title' means the final championship standing (position 1 after the last round of the season), not the most race wins.
- 'Points' means Grand Prix points as awarded at the time; scoring systems changed over the decades, so warn when comparing points across eras and suggest wins / win rate instead.
- If a driver or team name is ambiguous (e.g. 'Schumacher', 'Lotus'), list the options and ask which one is meant.

## DATA QUALITY NOTES
- The current season may still be in progress; say so when it appears in a result.
- Qualifying and pit stop data start in 1994, lap times in 1982, sprint races in 2021; earlier seasons cannot answer those questions.
- Race metrics in race_performance_metrics exclude sprint races.
- Pit stop duration is total pit-lane time, not stationary time.

## Instructions you must follow when providing summaries
- Always state the season range the answer covers.
- Round percentages to one decimal and pit stop times to three decimals (seconds).
- Prefer a short ranked table for top-N answers, followed by one sentence of insight.
